title.narrative: Kvinnor, fred och säkerhet, för en inkluderande agenda i Södra Kaukasus
Women, Peace and Security promoting an inclusive agenda

description.narrative:
Based on the mid-term review conducted during the spring 2024, Kvinna till Kvinna has revised the programme outcomes as well as slightly updated the programme objective /long term impact goal.
The overall (updated) programme goal is;
"A diverse and inclusive women's movement has improved holistic security and contributed to conflict transformation and women's rights in line with the WPS agenda"
The expected outcomes (updated) are;
Outcome 1 - Movement building: Inclusive and diverse women's rights movements are strengthened
Outcome 2- SGBV: Sexual- and gender based violence on individual and structural levels is prevented and addressed and SRHR promoted
Outcome 3 - Holistic Security: The safety and security needs of women's rights actors in countering shrinking civic space are addressed
Seven outputs (slightly updated) are identified which will facilitate results related to the above outcomes:
Output 1.1- Women's rights actors have access to resources and platforms for exchange, collaboration and bridging divides
Output 1.2- Internal capacity of women's rights actors is improved
Output 1.3- Women's rights actors participate and advocate on local, national, and/or international levels
Output 2.1- Women and girls have greater awareness of their rights pertaining to SGBV and SRHR
Output 2.2 -Women's rights actors engage decision makers to improve laws, services and protection of women victims/survivors
Output 3.1 - Tools, spaces, and resources are provided to enhance holistic security and risk mitigation
Output 3.2 -Partners and WHRDs have holistic security strategies in place
Advocacy Programme Component-
The three main outcome areas of the advocacy programme conneced to this contribution are interlinked and mirror the main outcomes of the regional programme. For each outcome area KtK has, in the application for the Advocacy Programme component, formulated a strategic advocacy objective, to which the activities will aim. The strategic advocacy objectives also resonate with the objectives of the Strategy for Stabilisation, Peace and Security.

Insatsen innebär stöd den lokala kvinnorörelsen i Armenien, Georgien och Ukraina. Organisationer får stöd till insatser som främjar fred och som inkluderar kvinnors perspektiv i samhällsbyggande och fredsbyggande arbete. Projektet består av tre delar: - Stärka kvinnorörelsen genom att skapa utrymme för erfarenhetsutbyte och nätverksbyggande - Motverka sexuellt och genusbaserat våld genom att adressera normer, sociala strukturer och lagstiftning - Stärka kvinnorörelsens säkerhetsarbete för att möjliggöra fortsatt arbete för inom området kvinnor fred och säkerhet, i en tid av minskat utrymme för civilsamhället i flera av programmets kontexter.

The initiative involves supporting the local women's movement in Armenia, Georgia and Ukraine. Organisations receive support for projects that promote peace and that include women's perspectives in community building and peace building work. The project consists of three parts: - Strengthen the women's movement by creating space for exchange of experiences and networking - Counteract sexual and gender-based violence by addressing norms, social structures and legislation - Strengthen the women's movement's security work to enable continued work for women in the area of peace and security, at a time of reduced space for civil society in several of the programme's contexts.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
KtK has during 2022 and beginning 2023 been focusing on the inception of the programme and on on-boarding new partners. This has included kick-off activities and capacity building activities for new partners as well as a participatory development of an updated results framework and MEL plan.
In general the support has facilitated women's rights movement building opportunities which has led to agreed joint agendas, for example when it comes work to prevent violence against women.
Another concrete example is the Armenian partner organisation Frontline Youth Network which is a pioneer in pushing a feminist and green peace agenda on an institutional level in Armenia. Despite a difficult year for Armenia and the Nagorno Karabakh context (full loss of control over Nagorno Karabakh and mass exodus of Armenians from the territory after the military attack of Azerbaijan in September 2023), this organisation stood by their values and continued to push for peace education curricula to be introduced in schools in Armenia. They have produced a toolkit for peace education and continue to work on its integration on an institutional level with the Ministry of Education in Armenia.
It is evident that the support has given opportunities for local women's organisations to participate in policy dialogue, advocacy, decision-making and conflict transformation processes. KtK with partners have also been strong when it comes to advocacy towards the EU. As an example KtK was asked to submit input to the EU Annual Country Report 2023 on Georgia, in the framework of the Enlargement Package.
Further, all supported partner organisations have been working on access to fair economic opportunities and justice for marginalized women and girls.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
